c0000005.name: Access violation
c0000005.meaning: it tried to use memory it wasn't allowed to

c0000409.name: Stack buffer overrun
c0000409.meaning: it found its own memory damaged and stopped itself

c0000374.name: Heap corruption
c0000374.meaning: its memory got damaged (often mods, overlays or a bug)

c00000fd.name: Stack overflow
c00000fd.meaning: it ran out of stack space (usually a bug)

c000001d.name: Illegal instruction
c000001d.meaning: the CPU met an instruction it can't run, which can point to an unstable overclock or undervolt

c0000096.name: Privileged instruction
c0000096.meaning: the CPU refused an instruction, possibly an unstable overclock

e0434352.name: .NET exception
e0434352.meaning: it ran into an error it didn't handle

80000003.name: Breakpoint
80000003.meaning: it stopped itself on an internal check

c0000142.name: Failed to start
c0000142.meaning: it couldn't start (often missing files or runtimes)

124.name: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
124.reason: The hardware reported an error it couldn't recover from, usually an unstable CPU or RAM.
124.advice: Undo overclocks and undervolts (XMP/EXPO and Curve Optimizer included), update the BIOS, and check temperatures.

101.name: CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT
101.reason: A CPU core stopped responding, commonly an unstable CPU overclock or undervolt.
101.advice: Reset CPU tuning (PBO, Curve Optimizer) to default and update the BIOS.

133.name: DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION
133.reason: A driver took too long to answer, often a storage, network or chipset driver.
133.advice: Update the chipset, storage and network drivers, and the SSD's firmware.

116.name: VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE
116.reason: The graphics driver stopped responding and couldn't be restarted.
116.advice: Update or clean-install the graphics driver, undo graphics card overclocks, and check its temperatures.

119.name: VIDEO_SCHEDULER_INTERNAL_ERROR
119.reason: The graphics scheduler hit an error, usually the graphics driver.
119.advice: Update or clean-install the graphics driver.

1a.name: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT
1a.reason: Windows found its memory bookkeeping broken, often faulty or unstable RAM.
1a.advice: Turn off XMP/EXPO to test, and run Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86.

50.name: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
50.reason: Memory that should always be there wasn't: bad RAM or a faulty driver.
50.advice: Test the RAM (XMP/EXPO off) and update drivers.

4e.name: PFN_LIST_CORRUPT
4e.reason: Windows' list of memory pages got damaged, often the RAM.
4e.advice: Test the RAM and turn off XMP/EXPO to check.

3b.name: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
3b.reason: A system service or driver crashed.
3b.advice: Update Windows and your drivers (graphics and anti-cheat especially).

7e.name: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
7e.advice: Update drivers; recently installed software is a common cause.

d1.name: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
d1.reason: A driver used memory it shouldn't have.
d1.advice: Update the network, audio and graphics drivers.

a.name: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
a.reason: A driver or the hardware used memory it shouldn't have.
a.advice: Update drivers; test the RAM if it repeats.

9f.name: DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
9f.reason: A driver failed while the PC went to sleep or woke up.
9f.advice: Update the chipset and graphics drivers; try turning off Fast Startup.

ef.name: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
ef.reason: A part of Windows that must keep running stopped.
ef.advice: Run 'sfc /scannow' and check the system drive's health.

7a.name: KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR
7a.reason: Windows couldn't read part of itself back from the drive.
7a.advice: Check the system drive's health (Kelvra → System) and its cable.

139.name: KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE
139.reason: Windows found damaged data in the kernel, usually a driver or RAM.
139.advice: Update drivers and test the RAM.
